docs.title: Aidus Agentus for FontLab 9
docs.text:
Aidus Agentus adds an AI chat dock inside FontLab 9. You can ask about the current glyph, inspect fonts and metrics, change spacing, or generate and run FontLab Python code. Responses stream into the dock. The selected AI provider receives your prompts and the tool results used by the agent; use a disposable font for your first editing experiments.

The FontLab plugin runs in the host's Python 3.11/PythonQt environment. The AI brain runs in a separate Python 3.13+ process, using AgentPool 2.8.8. Installing AI libraries into FontLab's embedded Python is unnecessary.

Read Configure Aidus Agentus for the short setup guide, architecture for the process/tool boundaries, and troubleshooting when something fails.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Use installation, configuration, dock and ACP and development and limits. The complete existing guides remain available:

docs.title: Current acceptance
docs.text: The maintained host/brain split is retained. Active-editor/CurrentGlyph preservation, M1–M11, provider authentication, dock lifecycle, writer history/persistence and operational brain cutover still need their separately recorded acceptance. Legacy repository retirement is already verified; it does not qualify these workflows. These source/build previews do not establish native or published operation.

docs.title: Configure Aidus Agentus
docs.text: Install the host and separate Python 3.13 brain first (README). Run Aidus Agentus > Open Configuration in FontLab's Scripts menu. It opens the loaded file, or creates a small template at ~/.config/aidus_agentus/config.json. If no valid config loads but a file exists, it opens that file for repair. Existing contents are preserved. Edit in a text editor and save as UTF-8 JSON (double quotes, no comments).

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
Replace the interpreter path with the brain environment's actual Python path:

{
  "python_exe": "/absolute/path/to/brain/bin/python",
  "api_keys": {
    "openai": "~/.config/aidus_agentus/openai-key.txt",
    "anthropic": "~/.config/aidus_agentus/anthropic-key.txt"
  }
}

The bundled agents use OpenAI and Anthropic. To use another provider, change the agent models as described in agents and models. Changing api_keys alone does not select a model.

docs.title: Keys in the JSON file
docs.text:
Key Default Meaning python_exe null External Python 3.13+ executable with the brain extra installed. AIDUS_PYTHON overrides it; otherwise a fontlab-aidus-python executable on FontLab's PATH is tried. Use an absolute path; ~ is expanded. api_keys {} Provider name to a private key-file path or env:VARIABLE_NAME. Never put the raw key here. File contents are stripped of surrounding whitespace. timeout_seconds 30 Positive number of seconds allowed without matching progress on an outstanding ACP request. Idle time does not count. core_path null Advanced: directory containing core_launcher.py (or legacy boot.py). Leave unset to use the installed launcher package. log_level "INFO" Retained compatibility field; currently does not change logging. The brain configures INFO logging on stderr.

The loader uses the first valid JSON object, in this order: aidus_config.json beside the installed packages (repository root when running source), that filename inside src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/plugin/, ~/.config/aidus_agentus/config.json, then ~/.aidus_config.json. It overlays that one file on defaults; files are not merged. Invalid/unreadable files are reported with their path and skipped, including files saved in another encoding. Their contents are never printed or replaced. Set AIDUS_CONFIG in FontLab's environment to use only that path; a missing/invalid explicit file falls back to defaults. _loaded_from, if shown by the loader, is diagnostic output, not a setting.

docs.title: Store provider keys safely
docs.text:
1. Outside the repository, create the two key files named in the example, using a text editor. Each file contains only its provider key. Do not paste keys into scripts, chat, screenshots or terminal commands.
  2. On macOS/Linux, restrict access in a terminal:
chmod 600 ~/.config/aidus_agentus/openai-key.txt ~/.config/aidus_agentus/anthropic-key.txt
  1. Alternatively use a mapping such as "openai": "env:MY_OPENAI_KEY". The variable must exist in FontLab's process environment; a terminal export does not update an already running GUI application. Without a mapping, the brain inherits canonical variables such as OPENAI_API_KEY from FontLab.

The plugin passes resolved mappings as OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, etc. to its child only; it does not add them to FontLab's parent environment or ACP messages. Provider aliases gemini and mistralai map to GOOGLE_API_KEY and MISTRAL_API_KEY. The external brain validates the selected models' credentials.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
In FontLab's Python console, check paths and key availability without printing keys:

from fontlab_aidus_agentus.plugin.config import load_config, get_api_key
c = load_config()
print("Config:", c.get("_loaded_from", "defaults"))
print("Python:", c.get("python_exe"))
print("OpenAI key available:", bool(get_api_key(c, "openai")))
print("Anthropic key available:", bool(get_api_key(c, "anthropic")))

Shut down the dock with fontlab_aidus_agentus.shutdown() (import it first), then run Start Aidus Agentus and wait for readiness. Ask for a read-only list of open fonts. A True key check only confirms availability; a successful response checks authentication. Reconnect alone does not reload host JSON or mapped key files. See troubleshooting if it fails.

docs.title: Develop and test
docs.text:
./test.sh needs two environments: the brain (Python 3.13+, .venv) and a host-like one (arm64 CPython 3.11, .venv-host, like FontLab's own Python):

uv venv --python 3.13 .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e '.[brain,dev]' /path/to/fontlab_remopy-VERSION-py3-none-any.whl
uv venv --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none .venv-host
uv pip install --python .venv-host/bin/python pytest pytest-asyncio pytest-cov
uv pip install --python .venv-host/bin/python --no-deps /path/to/fontlab_remopy-VERSION-py3-none-any.whl
./test.sh          # extra arguments go to the brain run, e.g. ./test.sh -x -k config

The brain run measures coverage of all three packages; the host run repeats the plugin, launcher and installer tests on 3.11 without AI libraries. Tests use fakes of PythonQt, QProcess and fontlab, and a deterministic AgentPool TestModel: no provider calls and no live FontLab. Every test gets an empty HOME and no *_API_KEY variables, and the run stops if an aidus_config.json sits at the repository root. Menu-script tests check the scheduling contract, not timing in the real application. guides/manual-tests.md lists what only a person at FontLab can check.

Build with uv build. Wheels contain the runtime packages, prompts and tool definitions. The sdist also contains the menu scripts, user docs and tests. DEPENDENCIES.md explains the dependency pins.

The v0.2.0 migration's native verification is recorded in the v1.1.7 WORK.md and RELEASE.md. The 2026-10-16 native check (FontLab 9.0.9783) covered import from this checkout, the installer, the executor tools on an owned font and deterministic ACP roundtrips through the fallback executor and native MCP; it did not open the dock or run the menu scripts.

docs.title: Open acceptance
docs.text:
Active-editor/CurrentGlyph read and write preservation are separate. Automatic-layer metric refusal must precede setters/history, including equal values; an empty request remains successful. Source guards do not establish whole-font Undo/Redo or save/reopen. Keep all M1–M11 and four package-aware native scenarios in the manual guide. Provider key availability is separate from authentication. The dock has no model picker; Reconnect reuses host settings while shutdown/start reloads them. A timeout is an unknown outcome and never permission to replay a mutation.

Legacy retirement is complete; it supplies no new native, runtime CI or brain-cutover result. Historical missing-component CI remains historical. This documentation workflow builds only the locked site; it does not replace product tests or signed/release checks. Private Pages configuration, requests and deployment are owner-held.

docs.title: Run in FontLab
docs.text:
The root Aidus Agentus folder holds three thin .py entry scripts and a README for FontLab's Scripts menu. In this workspace the orchestrator links it into FontLab's Scripts folder. Elsewhere, copy the scripts with the installer from the host package (run it in a terminal, not in FontLab):

PYTHONPATH=~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host python3 -m fontlab_aidus_agentus.install install
PYTHONPATH=~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host python3 -m fontlab_aidus_agentus.install check

--user-folder selects another FontLab user folder. The installer writes Scripts/Aidus Agentus plus a manifest with the sha256 of each file it wrote. Your own files in that folder are kept. A script you edited, or a symlink in place of one, stops install before anything changes; uninstall removes only the unmodified files it wrote and the folder only if it is then empty. Each write or removal re-checks its file first, and an interrupted install is completed by the next run. A folder (or link) without a valid manifest is never touched. check prints JSON and exits 0 only when the scripts are current and the brain Python is configured. With a full pip install, the same commands are fontlab-aidus-install install|check|uninstall.

  1. Run Open Configuration to edit the host JSON file.
  2. Run Enable FontLab MCP, or enable Preferences > Aidus > Allow external MCP clients to control FontLab. The script enables/notifies the running listener; it does not save the full preference set.
  3. Run Start Aidus Agentus. It queues startup on FontLab's Qt event loop, then returns promptly. The separate brain may take longer to connect.
  4. Wait for the dock to be ready. Ask: "List the open fonts without changing them." A streamed answer verifies a provider call; a tool result also checks the FontLab connection.

To start directly from FontLab's Python console:

import fontlab_aidus_agentus
fontlab_aidus_agentus.run()
# Before starting again, or after editing host configuration:
fontlab_aidus_agentus.shutdown()

The menu launcher shows an existing dock instead of starting another child. Reconnect starts a fresh child and ACP session using the already loaded host settings. It discards pending requests and never replays an edit. After changing host JSON or key files, shut down and start again to reload them. Idle sessions stay connected. A response timeout means the outcome may be unknown; inspect the font before resubmitting an edit.

Chat entries are saved locally to ~/.config/aidus_agentus/history.json (newest 500 rows, at most 2 MB, messages cut at 20,000 characters) and reappear when the dock starts; Clear clears the dock and removes that file. There is no model picker in the dock. Metric edits made through the fallback tools are one Edit > Undo step ("Aidus: Set Glyph Metrics"). Brain warnings and errors appear in FontLab's Output panel as [Aidus brain] lines (at most 50 per brain process); if the brain exits with an error, the dock shows its exit code and last five messages.

docs.title: The dock (GUI)
docs.text: The graphical part is src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/plugin/ui.py: AidusAgentusDock, a PythonQt QDockWidget that docks left or right in FontLab 9 and is the only window Aidus adds. It has a status label (connected or disconnected), Reconnect and Clear buttons, a read-only chat transcript with a colour per role (user, assistant, tool call, tool result, error), a "Thinking..." indicator and a one-line input field. src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/plugin/main.py creates it, client.py feeds it streamed updates and transport.py owns the brain process. It runs in the host and uses no PySide2. The dock is chat only: there is no model picker or settings panel yet (see PLAN.md); configuration stays in the JSON file that Open Configuration shows.

docs.title: Code it can write: the FontLab package set
docs.text:
Aidus is the coding agent for the FontLab Python ecosystem, not only for the native fontlab module. The maintained package guidance describes which layer to target, with import names and one-line usage. Private prompts are not published here:

Package Aidus writes code for fontlab-echopy (echopy) The documented, typed fontlab, fontgate, fontpr and PythonQt shims that Aidus builds upon fontlab-fly (fly) Short aliases (fl, fg, tr, pr, qt, ap, qs, gp, fp, pens) in scripts fontlab-fontlabapp (fontlabapp) Dialogs, panels, drawing, reports and guarded edits; glyph-window painters pythonqtside Qt5 widgets with PySide2-style names on host PythonQt fontlab-glyport (fontlab_glyport) Running Glyphs.app scripts and plugins fontlab-fontport (fontlab_fontport) FontParts and UFO interchange fontlab-python-plugmix (current core: fontlabapp.plugins) Native Reporter APIs through fly.ap.plugins; overlays use flCanvas.appendPythonPainter (with an EditorPainters fallback) fontlab-python-pens (fontlab_pens) Font drawing pens through fly.pens fontlab-python-scriptmix Scripts-menu tools (a folder of scripts, not an importable package) fontlab-remopy (fontlab_remopy) Driving FontLab from an external process; also the bridge Aidus itself uses

Generated FontLab scripts use fontlab-fly >=1.3.0 and the needed providers in FontLab's scripting environment. Native APIs use fly.fl, dialogs use fly.ap, and other providers use their Fly aliases. Missing packages need installation; Aidus reports the requirement instead of generating direct provider imports. The separate AI brain does not need Fly merely to generate these scripts. Generated code runs through the native MCP run_python tool or the fallback run_fontlab_script; neither installs packages. To see what a given FontLab session can import, run open -a "/Applications/FontLab 9.app" run_in_fontlab/check_aidus_in_fontlab.vfpy (or open it in FontLab). It writes a JSON report (AIDUS_LOAD_CHECK sets the path) and only imports.

docs.title: External ACP clients
docs.text: The brain also provides fontlab-aidus-acp (alias aidus-core) for stdio ACP protocol version 1. It is not an HTTP server. FontLab must be running with native MCP available for an external editor to control fonts; the fallback executor is provided by the embedded dock. The host JSON credential mappings are applied by the plugin, so external clients must supply their own provider environment. See architecture.

docs.title: Automatic-layer metrics
docs.text: set_glyph_metrics refuses explicit width or sidebearing assignments to native automatic layers before setters or history notifications. This includes equal values: the previous no-op path still invoked setters. An empty request remains successful. This source guard does not qualify the current-glyph read path or whole-font Undo/Redo preservation; native acceptance remains open.

docs.title: Install from this checkout
docs.text:
You need FontLab 9, uv, and access to the FontLab Remopy wheel. Download that wheel first; replace the example wheel path below with its actual path. These commands run in a terminal at this repository's root.

  1. Install the lightweight host package into a dedicated folder:
uv pip install --python 3.11 --target ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host .
# Optional: required for the Enable FontLab MCP menu script.
uv pip install --python 3.11 --target ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host --no-deps /path/to/fontlab_remopy-VERSION-py3-none-any.whl

Remopy's in-FontLab enable helper needs only the host's fontlab module; its external MCP dependencies belong in the brain environment.

  1. In FontLab's Python console, make that host folder importable:
import os, site
site.addsitedir(os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/host"))
import fontlab_aidus_agentus
print(fontlab_aidus_agentus.__version__)

This adds the path for the current FontLab session. Repeat after restarting FontLab, or have your FontLab environment setup add it on each launch. The Scripts-menu folder link alone does not install the package or add this path.

  1. Create the separate brain environment and install the real AI dependencies:
uv venv --python 3.13 ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/brain
uv pip install --python ~/.local/share/fontlab-aidus/brain/bin/python '.[brain]' /path/to/fontlab_remopy-VERSION-py3-none-any.whl

Remopy is supplied explicitly because it may be absent from the package registry. If you maintain a sibling fontlab-remopy checkout, use its path instead of the wheel. On Windows use the environment's Scripts/python.exe wherever these examples use bin/python.

  1. Set python_exe and provider-key sources in the host JSON file as described in CONFIGURE.md. The bundled manifest uses OpenAI for the copilot/analyst and Anthropic for the coder. Configure both providers, or supply your own manifest.

For an existing release, substitute its downloaded Aidus wheel for . and use '/path/to/fontlab_aidus_agentus-VERSION-py3-none-any.whl[brain]' for '.[brain]'. See RELEASE.md for v0.2.0 hashes and its historical verification. The new menu scripts require the current checkout's host package; v0.2.0 predates the installed launcher helpers. No PyPI installation is assumed.

See configuration and dock startup.

docs.title: Current English browser payload
docs.text:
The browser-component record binds the fly-january 0.2.0 and MaterialX 10.1.8 browser assets to exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps. Product terms above remain unchanged.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. The retained payload includes seven unchanged MaterialX assets, two MaterialX stylesheets rescaled by fly-january, and five assets from the fly-january wheel. Historical complete outputs remain recovery evidence; omitted helpers are not represented as currently distributed or relicensed.

The main source map retains 211 preferred sources, including 128 exact NPM source matches; the worker map retains 13 sources, including Lunr 2.3.9. The exact clipboard distribution embeds its dependencies; select, good-listener and delegate retain their upstream README MIT link and Zeno Rocha attribution, without invented standalone licence text or dates. CSS maps retain source names without embedded source bodies.

Material Design icons retain the Pictogrammers notice and Apache 2.0 icon terms or specifically stated underlying terms; code is MIT. Font Awesome Free retains Fonticons attribution and CC-BY 4.0 terms. Octicons retains GitHub's MIT notice; Lucide retains ISC and inherited notices. Of 45 observed ordered SVG path tuples, 43 match installed MaterialX icon path tuples exactly, including fontawesome/solid/caret-down.svg used by --md-version-icon. FontLab serves the shared menu and footer script. Adobe Fonts and Google Fonts serve typefaces and symbols, and jsDelivr serves PhotoSwipe 5.4.4 for image lightboxes. docs.title: How Aidus Agentus works
docs.text:
FontLab's embedded Python and modern AI dependencies have different interpreter requirements. Aidus keeps the UI and FontLab API calls in the host and runs AgentPool in an external child process.

FontLab 9 / Python 3.11 / PythonQt
  Scripts/Aidus Agentus/*.py -> fontlab_aidus_agentus.launchers (queued Qt action)
  fontlab_aidus_agentus.plugin: dock -> ACP client -> QProcess transport
                                           | stdin/stdout JSON-RPC
External Python 3.13+                       v
  fontlab_aidus_agentus.core_launcher -> boot -> fontlab_aidus_agentus.core.boot
  AgentPool 2.8.8 + ACP server -> selected AI provider
                            -> native MCP bridge -> FontLab
                            OR plugin tool request -> embedded executor
Location Responsibility src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/ Lazy public run()/shutdown(), Scripts-menu helpers and production ACP entry points. src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/plugin/ PythonQt dock, JSON configuration, request/session state, child transport and fallback FontLab executor. src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/core/ AgentPool manifest translation, provider models, ACP service and role-specific FontLab tool policy. fontlab-remopy (dependency) Native bridge discovery, authenticated MCP transport/relay and MCP enablement. Scripts/Aidus Agentus/ Three small menu scripts importing installed helpers; no package implementation or credentials. run_in_fontlab/ Developer checks and the PythonQt introspector, run inside FontLab by hand.

The base wheel has no runtime dependencies. fontlab and PythonQt come from FontLab. The optional brain extra installs the pinned AI stack in Python 3.13+. Imports of the public package or menu helpers never import AgentPool. Qt timers keep the menu run path short and perform host work on the GUI thread after the script returns. They do not move FontLab API calls into a worker thread.

docs.title: Tool selection
docs.text:
At brain startup, native MCP is selected only if Remopy finds a bridge and its tools/list probe returns a nonempty catalogue. Otherwise the brain imports the legacy plugin tools. That fallback needs the embedded dock/client to execute them in FontLab. Native tools use the bridge's own authentication; do not copy its token into configuration.

The copilot receives discovered native tools. The analyst receives only the explicit read-only allowlist; the coder receives that allowlist plus run_python. Fallback tools are taken from the agent manifest. Native run_python executes in FontLab's main Python environment; the fallback run_fontlab_script uses the plugin's restricted execution namespace. Inspect results and verify font edits.

docs.title: Agents and models
docs.text:
The bundled agents.yml declares:

Agent Bundled model Role fontlab_copilot openai:gpt-4o Main chat agent, including editing tools. fontlab_coder anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514 Script-oriented tools. fontlab_analyst openai:gpt-4o-mini Read-only tools.

These are bundled identifiers, not a promise of present-day provider availability. There is no dock model picker or automatic routing between these roles: the production entry point explicitly selects fontlab_copilot. AgentPool constructs the manifest's agents, so configure the providers referenced by that manifest.

To change models, copy src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/core/agents.yml and prompts/ together to a private configuration directory, preserving their relative layout. Set AIDUS_AGENTS_CONFIG to the absolute path of your copy in FontLab's process environment before starting Aidus. Edit each agent's model to an identifier supported by the installed PydanticAI version and configure the corresponding provider key. Keep fontlab_copilot present; changing only default_agent does not switch the production entry point. Keep the existing per-agent fields: type, system_prompt, tools, max_tokens and temperature. Prompt files resolve relative to the manifest. TestModel manifests support offline checks without provider credentials; see the production-entrypoint test.

docs.title: Environment reference
docs.text:
Set these in the process launching FontLab (or in its Python console through os.environ before startup). A terminal export alone does not change a running FontLab process. For an external ACP client, set them in that client's environment.

Variable Effect AIDUS_CONFIG Sole host JSON path; ~ is expanded. See CONFIGURE.md. AIDUS_PYTHON Overrides JSON python_exe. AIDUS_AGENTS_CONFIG External brain manifest path; use an absolute path, with no ~. AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP off disables discovery and selects fallback tools; any other value attempts discovery. AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND Explicit native bridge executable passed to Remopy discovery.

Host JSON is not the legacy core Settings class. Its core_host/core_port and .env assumptions do not configure the production stdio server.

docs.title: Sessions and local data
docs.text:
Transport uses newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over QProcess stdin/stdout; protocol version 1 is negotiated through ACP. Brain logging goes to stderr. Matching session progress renews an outstanding request deadline; idle READY sessions have no response deadline. A timeout leaves an unknown outcome.

Reconnect stops the child, clears pending/session state and negotiates a new session. It never replays a submitted request. Host settings and resolved key mappings are captured at bootstrap, so reload them with shutdown() then start. The dock saves displayed chat entries to ~/.config/aidus_agentus/history.json; Clear removes it. AIDUS_CONFIG does not relocate history. The brain uses in-memory session storage, which is independent of the dock's saved entries.

docs.title: External clients
docs.text:
fontlab-aidus-acp and aidus-core invoke fontlab_aidus_agentus.boot:main in the brain environment. An ACP-capable editor can launch that executable with no arguments, a suitable working directory and provider environment variables. There is no standalone terminal chat UI. Running the executable manually waits for protocol messages on stdin.

External clients must supply credentials themselves: the host JSON mappings are resolved by the embedded plugin, not by this executable. They also need running FontLab/native MCP for FontLab tool calls; fallback tools depend on an embedded client. Zed integration was an intended use of this interface; its interactive UI was not part of the recorded native release verification.

docs.title: Configure external agents for FontLab MCP
docs.text: Checked against FontLab 9.0.9780 source and a local Codex CLI on 2026-10-13, before the migration into this repository. OpenCode configuration follows its official documentation; the OpenCode connection itself was not tested. This guide changes no agent configuration; you apply it yourself.

docs.title: Connection and activation
docs.text:
Configure a local stdio MCP server. The agent starts a bridge subprocess; the bridge authenticates to the running FontLab application's local TCP server. There is no HTTP /mcp URL and no bearer token to put in agent configuration.

Start FontLab and enable Preferences > Aidus > Allow external MCP clients to control FontLab, then apply Preferences. Alternatively, run this inside FontLab with fontlab-fly >=1.3.0 and its providers installed in FontLab's scripting Python environment:

from fly import fl
fl.flPreferences().load({"mcp.enabled": True})
fl.flItems.notifyPreferencesChanged()

On macOS, this repository's helper can start FontLab and perform activation provided Remopy is already installed and importable in FontLab's host Python (see the README host --no-deps installation step). Installing Remopy only in the external brain/client environment is insufficient. The Fly API snippet above requires Fly in FontLab, but does not require Remopy.

open -a '/Applications/FontLab 9.app' "$PWD/run_in_fontlab/enable_fontlab_mcp.vfpy"

Run that command from this repository's root. Restart/reconnect the external agent's MCP connection after enabling the listener. Do not start a separate background bridge: the external agent owns the bridge process.

docs.title: macOS: Codex CLI
docs.text:
Native bridge registration:

codex mcp add fontlab -- '/Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp'
codex mcp get fontlab

Equivalent ~/.codex/config.toml section:

[mcp_servers.fontlab]
command = "/Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp"
args = []

The local codex mcp add --help confirms this stdio syntax, and codex mcp get fontlab currently reports this native bridge configuration as enabled. That verifies registration, not a tool call. Start a new Codex session and ask it to use FontLab's list_fonts tool to check execution.

docs.title: macOS: OpenCode
docs.text:
Add this to project opencode.json, or merge the mcp entry into the global ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json:

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "fontlab": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["/Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout": 15000
    }
  }
}

OpenCode's command is an argv array, so a path containing spaces remains one element. timeout is milliseconds. Use opencode mcp list to check discovery, then ask OpenCode to invoke list_fonts. These fields and the config locations are documented in OpenCode MCP servers and OpenCode configuration.

docs.title: Compatibility with FontLab build 9780
docs.text:
The native bridge in build 9780 can relay a successful result with isError: null, which strict MCP SDK clients reject. If that affects your agent, put the SDK normalization relay from fontlab-remopy in front of the bridge. The relay needs no LLM API key. Any Python 3.11+ environment with fontlab-remopy installed works, for example the Aidus brain environment from the README. The Codex configuration then becomes:

[mcp_servers.fontlab]
command = "/absolute/path/to/brain/bin/python"
args = ["-m", "fontlab_remopy.mcp.relay", "/Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp"]

For OpenCode, replace its command array with:

[
  "/absolute/path/to/brain/bin/python",
  "-m",
  "fontlab_remopy.mcp.relay",
  "/Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp"
]

Aidus Agentus has no relay of its own; use fontlab_remopy.mcp.relay. Keep the OpenCode type, enabled and timeout fields from the complete example. Native SDK and live ACP roundtrips through this relay were verified on 2026-10-13; no OpenCode tool call was verified.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
The inspected Windows FontLab 9.0.9780.0 installation contains MCP server code but does not include fontlab-mcp.exe. Therefore there is no working native stdio configuration for that installation until a matching Windows bridge is provided. Changing an agent config cannot supply the missing executable.

Once a matching Windows bridge is installed at the example path below, native Codex CLI registration from PowerShell is:

codex mcp add fontlab -- 'C:\Program Files\Fontlab\FontLab 9\fontlab-mcp.exe'
codex mcp get fontlab

Equivalent TOML uses a literal string for Windows backslashes:

[mcp_servers.fontlab]
command = 'C:\Program Files\Fontlab\FontLab 9\fontlab-mcp.exe'
args = []

For OpenCode use the same complete JSON object as on macOS, replacing command with this array (JSON requires doubled backslashes):

["C:\\Program Files\\Fontlab\\FontLab 9\\fontlab-mcp.exe"]

These Windows paths are conditional examples, not files found in the installed bottle. Use the actual path supplied with a compatible Windows bridge. Run FontLab, the bridge and the agent as the same Windows user so the bridge can read %LOCALAPPDATA%\FontLab\MCP\token.

For a macOS agent targeting CrossOver FontLab, a Windows bridge would need to run through Wine in the same bottle, so it resolves the Windows token. The current macOS bridge reads the macOS token and has no token-file override. Such a host-to-bottle configuration is not currently provided or verified. See the installation audit.

docs.title: Port number
docs.text:
The port is hardcoded to 47400 in both:

  • Proteus/common/mcp/mcpserver.cpp: MCP_PORT.
  • Proteus/mcpbridge/main.cpp: APP_PORT.

The current implementation has no preference, command-line argument or environment variable for changing it. There is no port field to add to the stdio agent configuration. Changing the port requires modifying and rebuilding both the listener and its bridge, or first implementing coordinated port configuration. If native macOS and CrossOver share localhost, they cannot both bind this port at once.

Bridge initialization alone is insufficient verification because it can succeed without contacting FontLab. Check tools/list, then a read-only list_fonts call against the intended application.

docs.title: FontLab MCP source and installation audit
docs.text: Inspected on 2026-10-13 against FontLab 9.0.9780 on the maintainer's machine, before the migration into this repository. Paths and versions describe that machine, not every FontLab distribution; re-check them against your build. No token contents, license data or credentials were copied into this repository. The complete historical audit remains in private recovery; it is not a site input.

docs.title: Source contract
docs.text:
Reference: the FontLab application source (Proteus/).

  • preferences/pref_fontographer.ui: Aidus's external-MCP checkbox is checkExternalMcp. It is distinct from built-in Chat and says changes take effect on applying Preferences.
  • preferences/pref_fontographer.cpp: the checkbox loads QSettings key mcp.enabled, whose default is false. Accept writes the same key. The external control is hidden in builds without MCP_SERVER.
  • common/mcp/mcpserver.cpp: MCPServer observes flItems::preferencesChanged. updateListener() opens localhost TCP port 47400 when the setting is true; disabling it closes the listener and disconnects existing external sessions. Setting a preference file externally while FontLab is running does not emit that notification.
  • pygate/pyflitems.h: the Python binding exposes fontlab.flItems.notifyPreferencesChanged(). The signal itself is not a callable attribute of the Python flItems.instance() wrapper. Use the public notification method, as in run_in_fontlab/enable_fontlab_mcp.vfpy.
  • common/flpreferences.cpp, flPreferences::saveDict() and loadDict(): extended save() includes the existing QSettings keys, including mcp.enabled once that key exists. load(dict) writes the supplied keys and reloads the preferences; it does not require a full snapshot. The running build returned 624 keys, including mcp.enabled, with no direct MCP attribute. The helper therefore uses the extended interface with a one-key dict, then notifies the MCP listener. It does not export the complete preferences or credentials.
  • common/mcp/mcpauth.h: application and bridge use the shared QStandardPaths::GenericDataLocation/FontLab/MCP/token file. The listener creates it; the bridge reads it. The token is 64 hexadecimal characters and is supplied in the TCP initialize request. A bridge can initialize its own stdio interface even while the application is unavailable: use tools/list to prove an authenticated application connection.
  • mcpbridge/main.cpp: the bridge connects lazily to 127.0.0.1:47400, reads the platform's token, initializes the application connection, and relays requests. Its native connection timeout is 5 seconds and read timeout 60 seconds. It does not start the application, change Preferences, expose HTTP, or accept a token-file override.
  • common/mcp/mcptools.cpp: journaling reads result["isError"] through the mutable Qt JSON subscript. This inserts a null member when a successful result omitted the optional error flag. The live build demonstrated that wire value; Aidus's SDK relay removes only this null member. The underlying source remedy would be reading through result.value("isError"); the FontLab checkout was not changed by this Aidus task.

docs.title: macOS installation
docs.text:
• Application: /Applications/FontLab 9.app.
  • Bundle identifier: com.fontlab.fontlab9.
  • Version: 9.0.9780, bundle build 9780, from Contents/Info.plist.
  • Bridge: /Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp.
  • Shared token path: ~/Library/Application Support/FontLab/MCP/token; its existence was verified, without reading its value into the report.
  • The local development bridge is Proteus/mcpbridge/fontlab-mcp. mcpbridge.pro builds a Qt Core/Network console program; build_universal.command checks the macOS arm64/x86_64 build.

Preferred activation is in the application: launch the .vfpy helper with open -a, then reconnect Aidus. This uses Qt's current application settings namespace and emits the listener's notification. Avoid using defaults write as the activation mechanism: it does not notify a running listener, and a subsequent Preferences apply can overwrite an externally changed value.

Aidus (through fontlab-remopy) discovers and starts the bridge automatically. Running the executable manually is useful for a protocol client, but is not an activation step.

docs.title: CrossOver Windows installation
docs.text:
The dated CrossOver observation used a private bottle. Its host paths and directory inventory are omitted here. The Windows installation path below is a conventional example, not a disclosure of a current installation:

C:\Program Files\Fontlab\FontLab 9\FontLab 9.exe
  • The uninstall metadata in the bottle's system.reg reports FontLab 9 version 9.0.9780.0 and that installation directory.
  • The executable is a Windows PE application, accompanied by python311.dll, PythonQt-Qt5-Python3.11.dll, PythonQt_QtAll-Qt5-Python3.11.dll, Qt 5 Core, Gui, Widgets, Network, Xml, Svg, Concurrent and PrintSupport DLLs, plus Qt plugins, translations and Resources.
  • This embedded Python 3.11 is for native FontLab scripting. The Aidus brain requires a separate modern Python 3.13+ environment. A macOS .venv/bin/python is not a Windows executable that a Wine QProcess can launch.
  • The dated application data directory observation was at C:\users\crossover\AppData\Local\FontLab\FontLab 9, containing Autosave and Licenser. Qt's shared MCP token location is separate: %LOCALAPPDATA%\FontLab\MCP\token. This follows Qt's documented GenericDataLocation defaults; operating-system configuration can change the actual writable location.
  • The Windows executable contains the mcp.enabled, MCP authentication, tools/list and external-client preference strings. This is evidence that MCP code is present; it is not proof that the listener is currently enabled.
  • The bottle's user.reg had no mcp.enabled entry during inspection, and the expected Windows MCP token file was absent. No Windows live MCP connection was claimed.
  • A recursive installation inventory found no MCP bridge file, including no fontlab-mcp.exe, and no packaged fontlab_python_mcp_spec.md.
  • CrossOver drive mappings and host-home access are private installation details, omitted from this guide.

The helper now imports Remopy. It requires Remopy installed and importable in Windows FontLab's embedded Python, not only in the separate brain environment. The historical file-access observation does not establish that dependency.

To activate Windows FontLab, run that helper with this prerequisite satisfied or use Preferences > Aidus and apply the external-MCP checkbox. That enables the listener, but the inspected distribution still needs a matching Windows stdio bridge for a Windows brain/client. Do not point a Windows QProcess at the macOS bridge. Do not assume the macOS bridge can authenticate to Wine FontLab: it reads the macOS token, while Windows FontLab uses the bottle's token. The current bridge has no argument to select another token file.

Both applications use localhost port 47400. If macOS and Wine share that port, only one can listen; use one target at a time and verify authenticated tools/list rather than identifying the application by an open port alone. Concurrent Windows/macOS MCP service and a host-to-Wine transport adapter were not implemented or verified in this task.

docs.title: Acceptance evidence
docs.text:
• Native embedded Python imported the updated Aidus ACP client and produced initialize, session/new, and session/prompt requests.
  • The running macOS server exposed 46 tools.
  • The normalized SDK connection completed read-only list_fonts successfully.
  • A complete live ACP client → Aidus brain → native macOS MCP → assistant response roundtrip passed, with no plugin executor invocation and clean EOF shutdown. AgentPool registered all 46 copilot tools and 20 analyst tools.
  • The activation binding flItems.notifyPreferencesChanged() was verified in the live embedded Python environment, and the helper was run in FontLab.
  • Automated tests cover active SDK MCP execution, inactive plugin fallback, role restrictions, startup deadlines, null-error normalization and clean process shutdown. They use deterministic models and do not edit fonts.

docs.title: Direct and extended preferences
docs.text:
These examples require fontlab-fly >=1.3.0 and its providers in FontLab's scripting Python environment. Prefer direct access when FontLab exposes an attribute, for example:

from fly import fl
preferences = fl.flPreferences()
preferences.generalDarkGlyph = not preferences.generalDarkGlyph
fl.flWorkspace.instance().updateActiveViewport()

The extended dict interface also supports the following snapshot/edit/load pattern. For this particular display setting, the direct attribute above is preferred; the example illustrates how the extended interface works:

preferences = fl.flPreferences()
prefd = preferences.save()
prefd["general.dark_glyph"] = not prefd["general.dark_glyph"]
preferences.load(prefd)
fl.flWorkspace.instance().updateActiveViewport()
profiles = prefd.get("profiles", tuple())

The latter follows the documented snapshot/edit/load pattern; profiles is the tuple of custom export profiles. MCP activation can use the smaller partial dict below because the source confirms loadDict() only writes supplied keys:

from fly import fl
fl.flPreferences().load({"mcp.enabled": True})
fl.flItems.notifyPreferencesChanged()

The viewport update in the display-preference example is unrelated to the MCP listener; activating MCP needs the preferences notification, not a viewport refresh. Avoid saving a full preference snapshot to a report: it can include private application settings.

docs.title: FontLab MCP in Aidus Agentus
docs.text:
When the brain starts, it checks FontLab's native MCP server. If the bridge returns a non-empty tool catalogue within eight seconds, the agents use native MCP. Otherwise they fall back to the plugin executor and its sandbox. A bridge that only initializes has not reached FontLab: discovery needs tools/list.

Bridge discovery, the authenticated transport and the SDK relay live in fontlab-remopy; Aidus calls them (src/fontlab_aidus_agentus/core/fontlab_mcp.py).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Install the brain environment as in the README. Remopy must be installed there. The enablement menu/helper also needs Remopy installed and importable in FontLab's host Python; the brain installation alone is insufficient. Follow the README's host --no-deps installation step.
  2. Start FontLab 9 and enable Preferences > Aidus > Allow external MCP clients to control FontLab, or run Enable FontLab MCP from the Aidus Agentus Scripts menu.
  3. Reconnect Aidus so the brain checks the server again.

The menu script calls Remopy's enable_mcp(). It sets the mcp.enabled preference and calls fontlab.flItems.notifyPreferencesChanged(), which the listener observes. No FontLab restart or font edit is needed. Do not keep a Preferences dialog open with the old unchecked value and apply it later: that disables MCP again.

The standalone script run_in_fontlab/enable_fontlab_mcp.vfpy does the same in a FontLab session where the host can import Remopy (macOS, from the repository root):

open -a '/Applications/FontLab 9.app' "$PWD/run_in_fontlab/enable_fontlab_mcp.vfpy"

You do not need to run fontlab-mcp as a background service. The brain launches it as a child process and talks MCP over stdio. Started by hand, it just waits for JSON-RPC input; it does not start FontLab or enable access.

Aidus looks for the bridge in this order: AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND, then Remopy's FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND, fontlab-mcp on PATH, /Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp, then ~/Applications/FontLab 9.app/Contents/MacOS/fontlab-mcp. The bridge talks to FontLab over local TCP at 127.0.0.1:47400; it is not an HTTP server. It reads the per-user authentication token itself, so never copy a token into configuration.

For a development build, export the bridge path in the brain's environment:

export AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP_COMMAND=/path/to/your/build/mcpbridge/fontlab-mcp

Use a bridge that matches the running FontLab build. The variable holds one executable path, spaces included, not a shell command. If that explicit path is unavailable, Aidus uses the plugin backend; it does not try another bridge.

Set AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP=off to force plugin execution. The default is auto. Both are process environment variables. The host JSON configuration does not forward them to the brain.

The relay (fontlab_remopy.mcp.relay) drops an isError: null field from successful results. FontLab build 9780 sent that value, and strict SDK clients reject it. Real tool errors and RPC errors pass through unchanged.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• The copilot gets every tool the server reports, with its schema.
  • The analyst gets a fixed list of known read-only tools. Read/write tools, scripts and unknown future tools are left out.
  • The coder gets those inspection tools plus run_python.
  • The plugin shows native tool notifications without executing the operation again. Assistant text chunks are collected into complete chat rows.
  • Without MCP, the three plugin tools (get_current_glyph_info, set_glyph_metrics, run_fontlab_script) run through the ACP extension method fontlab/tool (_fontlab/tool on the wire). The plugin registry, validation and script sandbox still apply.
  • ACP uses protocol version 1 and slash-separated method names. Sessions stay in memory.

run_python runs in FontLab's main Python environment under its native MCP execution policy, not in the plugin sandbox. The server choice is fixed when the brain starts. If FontLab stops or disables MCP later, tools report errors; reconnect Aidus. A mutation that timed out is never replayed automatically.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
tests/ and tests/core/test_mcp_roundtrip.py start a real SDK stdio server and the production brain with a deterministic model. They cover the ACP client, MCP execution, plugin fallback, timeouts and process cleanup without a provider call or font edit. Run them with ./test.sh.

For a live check, enable MCP and ask Aidus to list open fonts. The brain's stderr logs starting_acp_server with backend: mcp or backend: plugin. Compare the returned font list with FontLab. The repository tests cannot prove that your FontLab installation has external MCP enabled.

See the source and installation audit and external-agent MCP setup.

docs.title: Manual checks in FontLab
docs.text:
The automated suite (./test.sh) mocks FontLab and PythonQt. These checks cover native behavior that needs a running FontLab 9. Ported from the legacy repository's tests/MANUAL_TESTS.md and docs/INTEGRATION_TESTS.md, with authentication/timeout scenarios retained from docs/TESTING.md. These are acceptance targets, not a record of passing native results.

Use a dedicated test session containing only owned disposable copies of fonts. Record the actual FontLab build, host/brain package versions and loaded paths. Keep settings/history tests in an isolated test account; never clear an owner's chat history or change their credentials. Edits made by the agent are real.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Install the host package and the brain environment as in the README, and set python_exe (CONFIGURE.md).
  2. Make the Aidus Agentus Scripts-menu folder available: either the orchestrator's link, or fontlab-aidus-install install (check with fontlab-aidus-install check).
  3. Open a disposable font and select one glyph.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
# Do this Expect 1 Scripts > Aidus Agentus > Start Aidus Agentus The script returns at once; a dock appears; no traceback in the Output panel. 2 Watch the dock status It reaches a ready state. The brain may take several seconds; native MCP discovery can take up to eight. 3 Run Start Aidus Agentus again The existing dock is shown; no second brain process starts. 4 Ask "List the open fonts without changing them." A streamed answer that matches FontLab's open fonts. 5 Ask for the metrics of the current glyph Width, LSB and RSB match the Glyph panel. 6 Select the plugin backend as described below; ask to set an ordinary, non-automatic glyph layer's width to 700 The width changes once. Edit > Undo ("Undo Aidus: Set Glyph Metrics") restores it; Redo reapplies it. Verify complete font preservation, not only width. 7 Ask to run a script that prints the glyph count The count matches the font. 8 Close all fonts, then ask for current glyph info A readable error, no traceback; the dock stays usable. 9 Quit the brain (or wait for an error), then click Reconnect Reconnect is enabled only when disconnected or in error. A fresh session starts; pending requests are discarded, never replayed. 10 Ask for all glyphs with Unicode values (200+ glyphs); compare the displayed output with the actual tool result Output streams; the dock scrolls; FontLab stays responsive. Check live display separately from the bounded saved-history policy below. 11 Select a non-Latin glyph and ask about it Names and characters display correctly. 12 Switch FontLab between light and dark themes The dock stays readable in both. 13 Send messages, run fontlab_aidus_agentus.shutdown(), start again Earlier messages reappear (the newest 500 rows of ~/.config/aidus_agentus/history.json). 14 Click Clear The dock empties and history.json is removed. 15 Scripts > Aidus Agentus > Enable FontLab MCP, run fontlab_aidus_agentus.shutdown(), start again, ask to list open fonts The Output panel confirms enabling; the dock shows a list_fonts tool row, which only the native MCP catalogue provides. 16 Set python_exe to a Python without the brain extra, start again The Output panel shows [Aidus brain] lines and the dock shows the brain's exit code with its last messages. Restore python_exe afterwards. 17 Scripts > Aidus Agentus > Open Configuration The active JSON opens in your editor; an existing file is never rewritten.

After a timeout, the outcome of an edit is unknown: inspect the font before asking again.

docs.title: Backend and preservation controls
docs.text:
For check6, set AIDUS_FONTLAB_MCP=off in the dedicated FontLab process before starting Aidus. Shut down and start again after changing the environment; retain the brain's backend: plugin evidence. A natural-language request alone does not prove which tool ran: record the exact fallback tool call and arguments. Run a separate native-MCP case with discovery enabled and recorded backend: mcp. Do not assume native tools use the plugin's Undo label or history implementation.

For either writer path, compare the full owned font before, after, Undo, Redo and save/reopen, including unrelated glyphs, metadata and dirty state. Test an explicit metric assignment to an automatic layer separately: the candidate plugin guard must refuse before setters/history. Glyph-info read preservation and native writer qualification remain pending; a plausible metric value is insufficient evidence.

docs.title: Restored migration scenarios
docs.text:
The archived checklists also require these distinct cases. Keep failures visible; replacing a failed native check with a mock test does not complete it.

ID Do this Acceptance evidence M1 With an owned font open, leave no current glyph and request glyph info. Separately test zero chart selection while a current glyph still exists. No-current-glyph returns a readable refusal and leaves the font unchanged. Record selection and current-glyph states separately; zero selection alone does not prove no current glyph. M2 During a slow read-only response, change glyph selection, scroll the chat and resize the dock. Each action remains responsive; no crash or duplicate request. Record which glyph the tool actually inspected. M3 Disconnect only the identified test brain process; try to send a message. No edit is queued for later replay. The error is readable, visually distinct and provides connection/reconnect guidance; record any missing presentation as a failure. M4 Send several messages, close/hide the dock, reopen it through the Scripts menu. Then separately run full shutdown/start. Compare message content and scroll position in each lifecycle; one dock/brain only. Closing a dock is not equivalent to shutdown. M5 Send a harmless prompt, then a follow-up referring to its answer. Both turns appear and the response uses the current session context. Saved display history alone does not establish restored model context. M6 While a read-only response is pending, attempt a second submission. Input is disabled or the submission is clearly refused; no overlapping/replayed request or lost first response. M7 In an owned temporary user folder, install/check/uninstall the menu scripts and reopen the menu. Only installer-owned unmodified files disappear; unrelated files and edited scripts are preserved/refused. Use the current installer subcommands, not the archived flags. M8 Inspect installed host and brain versions/paths using the troubleshooting guide. Record actual package identities and any compatibility warning. The old status-bar/About version-display requirement remains unverified; package metadata is a separate check, not proof of that UI feature. M9 Shut down Aidus; separately quit the dedicated document-free FontLab session. The identified brain process exits in each case, with no orphan child. Do not kill unrelated Python processes. M10 Use a disposable brain configuration with required provider credentials deliberately absent. A clear startup/request authentication failure reaches the dock, with no secret values or native mutation. Host-side key-check deferral does not prove this provider behavior. M11 Use a controlled slow read-only response and a short positive timeout_seconds in the isolated configuration. Timeout is surfaced; reconnect creates a fresh session without replay. Retain the request outcome as unknown until reconciled. A client timeout does not prove native execution stopped.

The old five-second brain initialization and automatic ten-second reconnection expectations are not current promises. Measure startup separately from the short menu action, and use the explicit Reconnect control after a failure.

docs.title: Live display versus retained history
docs.text:
Check a response with known start/end markers both while displayed and after shutdown/start. The current dock displays incoming complete message text; saved history keeps at most500rows and a bounded JSON payload (2MB), with each message cut after20,000characters and marked … [truncated]. Verify the marker and retained newest rows, rather than claiming the archived unlimited-retention requirement still holds. Record any missing live output separately from expected history truncation. Capture only owned fixture content in evidence.

Record pass/fail/held per case, actual build/package/backend identities, fixture hashes, observed output and cleanup results. Historical v0.2.0 evidence does not clear these current native acceptance targets.

docs.title: Troubleshoot Aidus Agentus
docs.text:
Start with FontLab's Output panel and the dock's error messages. Never paste provider key values or private chat history into a report.

Symptom Check / fix Menu script says to install/update the package Install this checkout's host package, then add its host folder to FontLab's Python path as in README. Installing only in the brain environment does not install the host. The v0.2.0 wheel predates the new launcher helpers. fontlab-remopy is missing during installation Supply the downloaded Remopy wheel or a maintained Remopy source checkout explicitly alongside '.[brain]' / '.[brain,dev]'. It may be absent from the registry. Enable FontLab MCP reports a missing dependency Also install Remopy into the host folder using --no-deps; the native enable helper does not need external AI/MCP libraries in FontLab. Script says to run inside FontLab Run it from FontLab 9's Scripts menu. A terminal Python does not supply FontLab's PythonQt runtime. No dock appears / action reports RuntimeError Set python_exe to an existing external Python 3.13+ executable; check AIDUS_PYTHON is not overriding it. Watch Output after the queued action runs. Brain exits with an import error Install the declared brain extra into that exact interpreter. Keep the verified dependency pins in pyproject.toml; the host's Python 3.11 cannot run AgentPool. Configuration edits have no effect Check _loaded_from using CONFIGURE. A package-local file may take priority. Shut down and start the dock again; Reconnect reuses host settings/key mappings. Configuration is skipped as invalid or not UTF-8 Output identifies the affected path and reason. Open that file in a text editor and save a UTF-8 JSON object, with double quotes and no comments/trailing commas. Open Configuration can open an existing invalid file for repair when no valid file loads; it never replaces the original contents. With AIDUS_CONFIG, an invalid file produces defaults. Open Configuration does not show an editor Its path is printed in Output. Open that file in a text editor yourself; a system association for JSON is required for automatic opening. Existing content is never replaced. Key check is false / provider rejects a request Check private file existence, permissions and env: spelling without printing contents. Variables must be in FontLab's environment. A true availability check does not prove the key/account/model is valid. Missing Anthropic credentials despite an OpenAI copilot The bundled manifest also constructs an Anthropic coder. Configure both providers or copy and edit the manifest to use your chosen provider for every agent. Model is unavailable / wrong model responds Edit your private manifest and set AIDUS_AGENTS_CONFIG to its absolute path. The dock has no model picker; production selects fontlab_copilot. Dock connects but native MCP is unavailable Enable external MCP access in FontLab Preferences > Aidus, check the bridge and running FontLab, then Reconnect. Native discovery can take up to eight seconds before fallback. Brain termination outcome unknown Shutdown retains the process and dock; reconnect refuses to start a replacement until exit is confirmed. Inspect the identified brain process and wait for its completion signal, or retry shutdown after reconciliation. Do not treat a failed wait as proof that an edit stopped. Response timeout / disconnected during an edit Inspect the font before retrying; an edit might already have happened. Reconnect starts a fresh session and never replays edits. Increase positive timeout_seconds only if requests need more time. fontlab-aidus-acp appears silent in a terminal It is a stdio protocol server waiting for an ACP client, not an interactive chat command. Ctrl-D / EOF shuts it down.

docs.title: Check the two installations
docs.text:
In FontLab's Python console:

import fontlab_aidus_agentus
print(fontlab_aidus_agentus.__version__)
print(fontlab_aidus_agentus.__file__)
from fontlab_aidus_agentus.plugin.config import load_config
c = load_config()
print(c.get("_loaded_from", "defaults"), c.get("python_exe"))

In a terminal, using your configured brain interpreter:

/absolute/path/to/brain/bin/python -c 'import sys, importlib.metadata as m; print(sys.version); print(m.version("fontlab-aidus-agentus")); print(m.version("agentpool")); import fontlab_remopy'

Do not print the complete config or child environment: they can contain private paths or inherited secrets. The retained check_health() helper checks manifest shape; it does not prove provider authentication, native MCP reachability or a working GUI. A successful read-only chat/tool request checks the actual connection.

docs.title: Verification boundaries
docs.text: The repository suite runs without FontLab, using mocks and a real AgentPool TestModel ACP subprocess. Its launcher tests verify imports, script size, deferred work, failure guidance and configuration preservation. Actual dock rendering, PythonQt timers, system editor associations, Scripts-menu discovery and the five-second deadline still need verification in the target FontLab build. The historical v0.2.0 native results in RELEASE.md cover that release, not these new scripts. CrossOver/Windows and interactive external-editor behavior are not established by those macOS checks.
